NextItNet uses causal dilated convolutions and residual connections. Calculate receptive-field width from actual convolution layers: R = 1 + Σ(kℓ−1)dℓ for stride 1. Two convolutions sharing dilation d contribute 2(k−1)d; the authors’ implementation instead uses d and 2d per block, giving R = 1 + 3(k−1)Σd across blocks. With k=3 and block dilations [1,2,4], R=43. Inspect the supplied architecture before applying either formula. [Original implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet/blob/master/ops.py).

Architectural inference: a suffix of length s≥R supplies identical final-position context to a deterministic, shared-weight causal backbone, provided padding states are handled consistently and normalization is positionwise. It adds no distinct contextual information. A shorter suffix can change features by removing reachable older interactions; an auxiliary loss or stochastic augmentation can change optimization even when contextual information overlaps. Cropping is therefore a training intervention, not evidence of intent or preference drift. NextItNet’s original motivation includes learning both short- and long-range dependencies. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163).

Suggested diagnostics within the single NextItNet model: compare validation predictions using full history, last item, and progressively longer suffixes; shuffle older interactions while preserving the suffix, then shuffle the suffix while preserving the last item. Ablate any jointly trained last-item shortcut and suffix auxiliary loss separately under matched training budgets. Report macro HR@10 and category/history-length breakdowns using fixed candidates. Separate inference perturbations from retrained ablations: perturbation losses can reflect distribution shift. Similar full-history and last-item performance suggests limited measured dependence on older context; it does not establish intent or absence of long-term preferences.
